f.title: Maintain a robust pharmacovigilance system to meet the Act and regulations
f.statement: To meet your responsibility for the requirements outlined in the Food and Drugs Act and regulations and clarified in Health Canada guidance documents (which also needs the help and commitment of your partners and personnel at all levels), you need a robust pharmacovigilance system, as it forms an integral part of Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP).

rows.quote: You are responsible for meeting the requirements outlined in the act and regulations and clarified in our guidance documents. You will also need the help and commitment of your partners and personnel at all levels. To meet these requirements, you need a robust pharmacovigilance system as it forms an integral part of Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP).
rows.review_note: Review: level Mandatory -> Recommended. The legal duty to comply with the regulations and apply GVP is already captured as Mandatory in the regulations page (HC-GUI0102-REGS-0001); this row keeps only the GUI-0102 expectation of a robust PV system ('you need', no must/shall). Statement reworded; categories reordered. Double-check: kept Recommended: 'you need' is an expectation, and the legal duty to comply is captured as Mandatory in HC-GUI0102-REGS-0001; statement recentred on the robust-system expectation. Below 90: the level is a judgement call (the quote opens with a statement of legal responsibility) and it partly restates REGS-0001.

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed; quote has 'you should' with its lead-in.

f.title: Have contractual agreements with group entities, PV service providers, label-named companies and cross-licensing MAHs
f.statement: At minimum, a contractual agreement should exist between the MAH and: global entities under the same ownership or corporate structure (unless processes are already outlined in corporate procedures); service providers outsourced to conduct pharmacovigilance activities on your behalf, such as literature searches, executing terms and conditions, post-marketing studies or risk minimization measures; external parties who will receive ADRs or safety data on your behalf; companies whose names or contact information are included in the physical or electronic product label or electronic platforms, such as the Canadian importer or third-party private labelers; and MAHs of cross-licensed products.
f.clause: Contractual agreements > Delegation of pharmacovigilance activities
f.exceptions: For global entities under the same ownership or corporate structure, not needed where processes are already outlined in corporate procedures.
f.processes: Partner & vendor oversight; Local PV interfaces

f.title: Include minimum elements in PV contracts: roles, effective date, products, definitions, exchange timelines
f.statement: Your contractual agreement or its annex, where applicable, should include, at minimum: roles and responsibilities of each party for each specific delegated activity; the effective date of the agreement; a list of products in scope; definitions of all relevant pharmacovigilance terms; and the timeline and scope of safety information to be exchanged.
f.clause: Contractual agreements > Elements of a contractual agreement on pharmacovigilance activities

f.title: Include minimum contract elements: subcontracting approval, audit rights, records, signatures, contacts
f.statement: Continuing the list of elements that your contractual agreement or its annex should include at minimum: a requirement for your written authorization if the third party subcontracts work to another party; your right and responsibility to audit third-party vendors according to your risk-based strategy; the third party's assistance in your audits and regulatory authority inspections; the need for the third party to provide all records and respond to questions related to the outsourced activities in a timely manner when requested; the need for record retention on activities conducted by the third party in accordance with regulatory requirements; dated signature or equivalent legally binding approval of the relevant officials from both parties; and contact information of both parties.

f.title: Consider risk-based contract terms: reconciliation, change control, information provision, metrics, impact communication
f.statement: Your contractual agreement or its annex should also consider, where relevant according to the risk of impact on your pharmacovigilance system: a reconciliation process for pharmacovigilance data, outlining the methodology and frequency, so that any missed communication about ADR reports or signals is addressed in a timely manner; a change control system governing changes to the pharmacovigilance system(s); requirements for you to provide the third party with the information needed to carry out the contracted operations; metrics for when both parties need to be notified of changes or deviations to the pharmacovigilance system; and communication of any potential impacts on pharmacovigilance activities between you and the third party.

f.title: Continue regulatory and GVP compliance during mergers, acquisitions and database migrations
f.statement: Compliance with the requirements set out in the regulations and the GVP principles in this guidance document must continue during transition periods such as a merger, acquisition or migration of pharmacovigilance databases.
